title: Agent cards
lede: An agent gets a card. A charge outside the policy gets declined. This sandbox demo does not verify which agent is calling.

title: Drop-in checkout flow
lede: Embedded card checkout on your own page.
script: Cadence is a social scheduler on Replit. Upgrade does nothing.
There is no payment system behind it.
Adding card payments usually means weeks in API docs. Here you connect Airwallex Drop-in.
Keep the card form on your own page. Keys stay server-side.
A webhook marks the account Pro after a sandbox payment.
Checkout on the product page. Card fields from Airwallex. No real money.

title: Invoicing in Slack
lede: Tag a Slack thread, get an Airwallex invoice.
script: What if you could invoice clients straight from Slack?
You agree on the price right there in the chat.
Once the client approves, you simply tag AirwallexBot.
The invoice is prepared right inside the conversation.
One click sends it by email and shares the payment link right here in Slack.
The client opens the link and gets a secure Airwallex payment experience.
Card, Apple Pay, Google Pay — whatever they already use.
And that's just one of the billing experiences you can build with Airwallex.

title: AI finance manager
lede: Text an agent that reads live Airwallex balances and can prepare payments.
script: What if you had an AI finance manager who actually knew your numbers? Not a dashboard. An AI finance manager you could just text.
So you could ask it what you have. And it wouldn't guess. It would pull your live balances, then work out your runway.
Then you could ask what's wrong this month. And it would tell you: a vendor whose spend has spiked, a supplier you've never paid, a card running way outside its normal pattern.
You could ask it to put your month-end together. Cash, spend, budget and anomalies.
And when you ask it to move money, it stops. It shows you the amount, the counterparty, the account it's coming from. Then it waits for you to say yes.
So what makes this possible?
Underneath, it's Airwallex AgentOS. That's where your balances, transactions, cards and payments come from, over one connection you authorize yourself.
Everything above that, you build. Your own tools alongside AgentOS. Runway, anomaly detection, budget variance, reporting.
And your own skills. The workflows and policies your agent follows. Like always preparing a payment, and waiting for a yes.
This example runs on Hermes. But nothing here is specific to Hermes. Any agent that speaks MCP can do this.
And getting it running is short. Install the pack, connect your own Airwallex account, point it at a Telegram bot.
This is one example of an agent built on Airwallex. Your tools. Your skills. Your experience.
Build yours now.

title: Allocard
lede: Company cards with dynamic spending limits. An agent sets them from budget rules.
script: Most finance tools make you work their way.
Your rules have to fit their settings page.
With Airwallex, you build your own. One that fits how your company actually spends.
So we built one.
It's called Allocard.
It hands out company cards, and nobody types in the limits.
Every limit is a rule, not a number.
So when a project's budget drops, the rules run again.
Limits follow the budget.
Below ten percent, the cards freeze.
Seconds later, the card has changed.
No ticket. No approvals. And it can show you why the limit is what it is.
Underneath, it's one call to Airwallex.
It sets the spending controls on the card.
We decide. Airwallex enforces.
So the limit is real.
The next charge over it simply doesn't go through.
Cardholders, cards, limits, card details, and a webhook for every charge and every decline.
Allocard is just one example.
Build the one that fits you.
